answer: Friction scoring accumulates per-identity costs from small pattern deviations. Each new identity must wander through a probabilistic challenge sequence whose expected work grows with cluster size, so an attacker pays rising compute per fake account. A marble of verified history grants discounted entry, making fresh identities expensive relative to seasoned ones, while repeat behavior near an oasis of trusted peers triggers higher scrutiny. Total cost scales superlinearly with Sybil count, pricing mass duplication above honest participation.
